justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a broadly stable near-term outlook with a modest upward drift over time. For the one-day horizon, I anchored close to the prevailing market level, assuming no major overnight catalysts and normal session-to-session continuity. The slight upward nudge in the one-week estimate reflects a mild positive drift assumption consistent with historical equity risk premium dynamics, while the one-month estimate continues that gradual drift, arriving at a round number that essentially implies slow, grinding appreciation rather than any decisive directional move. None of these estimates embed a strong macro view; they are largely mean-anchored with modest trend continuation.

The confidence interval widths expand predictably as the horizon lengthens, reflecting the square-root-of-time scaling of uncertainty that underlies most standard asset pricing models. At one day, realized volatility in broad equity indices tends to be contained barring specific shock events, so the interval is relatively tight. By one week, the interval widens to absorb the possibility of a Federal Reserve communication, an unexpected earnings surprise from a large-cap constituent, or geopolitical news. At one month, the interval is wide enough to encompass a meaningful macro data revision, a shift in rate expectations, or a change in market sentiment regime. Implied volatility levels in options markets at the time of my forecast also informed these widths, as did awareness that volatility itself is non-stationary and can spike quickly.

The most significant tail risks that could push outcomes outside my stated intervals include an abrupt shift in Federal Reserve policy signaling — particularly if inflation data surprised sharply in either direction — which could move markets several percentage points in a single session. A geopolitical escalation, a credit event in a systemically important institution, or a sudden liquidity disruption in Treasury markets could all produce moves well beyond my one-month confidence interval on the downside. On the upside, a surprisingly strong resolution to ongoing trade or fiscal policy uncertainty, combined with a soft landing narrative solidifying, could drive a sharp rally beyond my upper bounds. These tail scenarios are low-probability individually but collectively represent meaningful risk that my intervals, by construction, do not fully capture.
